_doc: DECISIONS-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-18): "Measure what we improve and improve what we measure." Every autonomous decision point declares the metric it optimizes; each decision it makes is logged with its predicted effect and later scored against the measured outcome (foundation/decisions.py, ledger ops/decisions/ledger.jsonl, outcomes ops/decisions/outcomes.jsonl; Worker-side points in D1 decision_log, 7 days then chain-archived). A code path marked `DECISION-METRIC: <id>` must name a registered point; a registered point's files must carry the marker; a decision-shaped function in a file with no marker must be on the shrink-only `uninstrumented` list (filed as Q-DECISION-COVERAGE-1). Runtime probe: `python3 -m foundation decisions --probe` (outcomes scored, not just logged). Public page: /decisions and /api/decisions. Consumers: foundation/decisions.py, doctrine/rules.json (rule every-decision-measured), site/worker.js, seed/worker/src/decisions.js, scripts/regen_generated.py.

points.name: Idea loop: which new spinoff ideas and loop-scope increases to queue
points.metric_says: 1 when the free-plan level is still below shed a day after the idea was queued
points.predict: 1 (the idea was priced inside the day's headroom, so the level should stay below shed)
points.why: An idea is queued only if its priced cost fits the free-plan headroom, so the outcome that proves the pick was sound is that the plan was not pushed to shed.

points.name: Spinoff launch: which queued app to launch next
points.metric_says: real uses of the launched app in its first 7 days (ops/spinoff/metrics.jsonl)
points.predict: the app's reach score (1 to 5), read as an ordinal prior of weekly uses; calibration shows how far it sits from measured uses
points.why: Launch order is the score reach x impact x feasibility; the measure of whether the pick was good is whether anyone used the app.

points.name: Work queue: which open item the executor takes next
points.metric_says: 1 when the picked item is closed (verified, merged or closed by its probe) inside one cycle
points.predict: 1 (driver order picks the item the loop expects to close inside one cycle)
points.why: Driver order exists to close the most valuable item fastest; an item that is picked and not closed is a measured miss in the priority function.

points.name: AI router: which model answers a call
points.metric_says: 1 when the chosen model's reply passed the deterministic quality gate and the task's own verify, else 0
points.predict: the model's learned pass rate for this kind of call (0.5 until it has 8 calls)
points.why: The router tries the cheapest free model with the best learned pass rate first; each call scores that choice immediately, so the learned order is calibrated by real replies.

points.name: Plussing: which improvement lever to pull
points.metric_says: 1 when the improvement the lever produced was kept after scoring (target moved, no guard worsened), 0 when it was reverted
points.predict: 1 (the ranked gap is expected to move its target)
points.why: The protected improvement budget is spent on the weighted largest gap; the measure of the choice is the share of changes that survive scoring.

points.name: Free-tier governor: ok, degrade or shed
points.metric_says: the largest share of any free-plan daily allowance in use at the next sample (must stay under 0.95, the shed line)
points.predict: the worst share at the time of the decision (a persistence forecast; the governor must beat it by acting)
points.why: The governor sets the level that throttles every loop; each level it sets is scored by whether the account stayed below the shed line.

points.name: Self-code finding: which sensed defect the agent files as work
points.metric_says: 1 when the item filed for the sensed finding is closed (fixed or verified) within the window
points.predict: 1 (the finding passed the rails, so its item should close inside a week)
points.why: Findings are ranked by score and filed within caps; the outcome that proves the pick was worth filing is that its item reached a closed state.

points.name: Outreach segment: which kind of organization the next introductions go to
points.metric_says: mean reply reward per contacted prospect in the chosen segment (accepted or meeting 1, question 0.6, acknowledgement 0.3, anything else 0)
points.predict: the segment's mean reward so far, or 0 for a segment never tried
points.why: The per-run cap is spent on one segment first; the pick was right when prospects in that segment answer, which is what the learner maximizes.

points.name: Work-queue second loop: whether to consolidate, throttle filing and boost closures this pass
points.metric_says: closed minus net filed over the last 7 days, read on the pass after the decision
points.predict: >= 0 (dedupe, batching and the executor boost bring weekly net inflow to or below closures)
points.why: FLOW-BALANCE-1: the only outcome that shows the corrective plan worked is that closures caught up with net inflow without closing anything to move the number.

points.name: Orchestrator: how a failed item is split into steps
points.metric_says: 1 when the planned run opened its pull request, 0 when it ended failed
points.predict: the share of earlier planned runs that opened a pull request (0.5 until 4 runs are settled)
points.why: ORCHESTRATE-1: a plan is only as good as the run it produces; scoring each accepted plan by whether its steps, review and fix rounds reached one pull request shows whether planning is working on the models the system can afford.

not_decisions.foundation/reposhape.py: plan batches a branch's changed files by class and path under a fixed size budget; the split is a deterministic computation with no alternatives to weigh
not_decisions.foundation/semrel.py: plan and classify map Conventional Commit types to a SemVer bump by a fixed table, with no alternatives to weigh
not_decisions.foundation/agents.py: route_authors maps author names to roles from environment variables, a fixed lookup with no alternatives to weigh
not_decisions.foundation/repostd.py: classify and desired compute a fixed standard: a branch's class from its pull requests and a repository's settings from one default block; nothing is weighed or chosen
not_decisions.foundation/boundary.py: decide looks a surface and action up in the boundary policy ledger, a deterministic rule with one allowed answer
not_decisions.foundation/branchsweep.py: plan_one derives the disposition of a branch from its merge state, a fixed table, and the sweep ledger records every outcome
not_decisions.foundation/conflicts.py: decide is a pure truth table over four booleans from the merge attempt, with no judgment or ranking
not_decisions.foundation/design.py: select matches the idea's words to a personality by keyword score, deterministically, and design experiments score the looks themselves
not_decisions.foundation/filing.py: plan fills a filing manifest from a fixed table, a mechanical transform whose result is identical on every run
not_decisions.foundation/ghmirror.py: plan is a pure diff between the docs/issues files and their GitHub mirror issues; the file always wins, so there is no alternative to weigh
not_decisions.foundation/seedadmit.py: The admission verdict is computed from probes and the year simulation against fixed thresholds in the kit; it chooses nothing among alternatives and has no outcome to score later.
not_decisions.foundation/seedlaunch.py: verdict and check compare boot-log stage statuses and ledger age against fixed required stages and a fixed age, a deterministic gate with one answer
not_decisions.foundation/thought.py: choose is a fixed rotation rule (a paper whose measured result changed goes first, else the one posted longest ago once repost_days have passed), with nothing weighed; what readers act on is learned by the reach loop's paper arm
not_decisions.foundation/triggers.py: plan lists each role's tick period from the heartbeat cron and role files, derived arithmetic with no choice
not_decisions.seed/worker/src/airouter.js: vendored copy of core/airouter; the routing decisions are logged and scored under ai-router by src/airoute.js and decisions.js
not_decisions.seed/worker/src/critloop.js: pickForRole takes the first role-matching item from the rank computed by foundation/prioritize.py, which carries the work-queue-priority metric
not_decisions.seed/worker/src/events.js: routeEvent looks an event name up in EVENT_TABLE generated from doctrine, a table lookup with no ranking
not_decisions.seed/worker/src/pace.js: rankRows sorts rows by the rank list already chosen by foundation/prioritize.py, which is the instrumented decision
not_decisions.seed/worker/src/contract.js: routesIn and contractRoute read a router's paths and match a request path against two fixed routes, a lookup with one answer and nothing to weigh
